reason: The sources provide multi-site cross-verified facts detailing Voyager 2's 1989 Neptune encounter, its weather discoveries, moon flybys, and later Hubble follow-ups.
story: In August 1989, NASA's Voyager 2 executed its final planetary flyby, swooping just thousands of miles above Neptune's north pole. At the outer edge of the solar system, where sunlight is only three percent of what Jupiter receives, scientists expected a frozen, quiet world. Instead, Voyager 2 discovered a violently dynamic atmosphere featuring a giant Earth-sized anticyclone named the Great Dark Spot, whipped by extreme winds. The probe uncovered rings, six previously unknown moons, and a highly offset magnetic field. Hours later, Voyager 2 zipped past Neptune's largest moon, Triton, revealing active ice geysers spewing dark plumes across a world trapped in a backward retrograde orbit. When the Hubble Space Telescope looked back in 1994, Neptune's Great Dark Spot had vanished entirely, proving that the ice giant's wild weather systems are constantly shifting.
angle: When Voyager 2 reached distant Neptune in 1989, it discovered an Earth-sized mega-storm called the Great Dark Spot, only for the entire storm to completely vanish by 1994.

claims.claim: Voyager 2 was launched in 1977 on a mission to explore the outer planets.
Voyager 2 conducted a flyby of Neptune in August 1989.
Neptune receives only 3 percent of the sunlight that Jupiter receives.
Voyager 2 discovered a giant atmospheric storm on Neptune named the Great Dark Spot.
Neptune's Great Dark Spot was roughly the same size as Earth.
The Great Dark Spot was an anticyclonic high-pressure storm system.
When the Hubble Space Telescope attempted to photograph the Great Dark Spot in 1994, the storm had vanished completely.
Voyager 2 discovered six previously unknown moons orbiting Neptune.
Proteus was one of the small moons discovered by Voyager 2 during its Neptune flyby.
Voyager 2 captured the first images of rings encircling Neptune.
Neptune's magnetic field is heavily tilted and offset from the planet's geometric center.
Triton orbits Neptune in a retrograde direction, opposite to the planet's rotation.
Triton is believed to be a body captured by Neptune from the Kuiper Belt.
Voyager 2 detected active geysers spewing dark material into Triton's atmosphere.
Voyager 2 made its closest planetary approach on August 25, 1989, passing thousands of miles over Neptune's north pole.

disputed: Exact top wind speeds on Neptune: S1 cites winds up to 1,300 mph (2,100 km/h) around storm edges, S3 cites wind speeds up to 1,000 mph, S2 notes winds up to 3 times stronger than Jupiter's, and S5 estimates storm winds around 328 ft/s (100 m/s). Attribute peak wind speeds generally as extreme supersonic speeds between 1,000 and 1,300 mph as measured during the flyby.
Exact count of Neptune's rings: S2, S4, and S6 state four rings were identified, while S3 describes a system of five rings. Attribute as a system of four to five dark rings.
